requirement_text: System operators want to minimize generation costs, operating costs, real-time adjustment costs, or market costs while satisfying power flow, security, voltage, line, and other constraints.
Users or operators need the power grid to operate safely under both normal and contingency conditions, especially considering line outages, generator outages, N-1 contingencies, and similar events.
Wind and photovoltaic generation are volatile and subject to forecast errors. Traditional deterministic OPF may lead to suboptimal, infeasible, or even unstable results.

After renewable generation and load change rapidly, the optimal solution from the previous time step may quickly become infeasible. Therefore, the model needs to update quickly and maintain feasible operation.
The system needs to reduce carbon emissions, improve RES utilization, and support energy transition goals.
Data centers and highly concentrated electricity loads may create strong local load growth and grid pressure. The model needs to identify local congestion, security issues, and capacity bottlenecks.

With the growth of electric vehicles, data centers, heating and cooling loads, and electrification demand, the system needs to manage peak loads and reduce local equipment and network overload pressure.
Distribution grid users need reliable power supply, fewer outages, reduced fault impacts, and less unserved energy.

During low-wind and low-solar periods, droughts, equipment failures, or high-load periods, the system needs sufficient generation, reserves, storage, or capacity mechanisms to meet demand and ensure supply security.

Cross-regional, cross-border, or multi-area interconnected systems need coordinated security analysis, capacity calculation, power flow utilization, regional reserves, and market clearing, so that local optimization does not cause cross-area congestion or security risks.

After high penetration of renewable energy and converter-interfaced resources, the system needs to consider dynamic stability, oscillations, loss of synchronism, low inertia, and protection actions, rather than only static economic efficiency.
High renewable variability requires ESS to absorb fluctuations, provide reserves, improve voltage stability, and participate in multi-period energy management.
In a market environment, OPF is not only used for cost minimization, but may also serve day-ahead markets, real-time markets, reserve markets, and profit maximization.
When distributed grids, user-side DERs, and loads participate in scheduling, nodes or users may be unwilling to share complete electricity consumption data.

requirement_name: Computational Speed / Online Tractability and Accuracy and Physical Feasibility
requirement_text: Real-world OPF needs to be completed within the time scale of market clearing, real-time dispatch, or voltage control. Approximate models and ML predictions are fast, but they may violate AC power flow and security constraints. Therefore, physical feasibility must be guaranteed.
Optimizing only continuous generation output is not enough. Microgrids or generator systems also need to decide unit on/off commitment states.

requirement_name: Line Congestion and Thermal Limit Management
requirement_text: Line capacity, thermal stability limits, and power flow violations are core issues in high-DER systems, load growth, and network reconfiguration.

DSOs/TSOs not only need flexibility resources to exist, but also need them to be activated at the right location, at the right time, and in the right quantity, and their effect must be visible at the service verification point.
Large power grids, complex ACOPF, SCOPF, multi-scenario, and multi-period problems are large in scale, and traditional solvers may not solve them within an acceptable time.

I need a real-time frequency-constrained OPF model for low-inertia modern power systems. As renewable energy and power-electronic devices are increasingly integrated, system inertia decreases, and generator trips can more easily cause rapid frequency drops. Therefore, OPF should not only consider economic cost and conventional power flow constraints, but also include RoCoF and frequency nadir as frequency security indicators in dispatch decisions. However, accurate frequency response calculation requires complex differential-algebraic equations or EMT simulation, which is too slow to be directly embedded into real-time OPF. Traditional linearized RoCoF constraints or simplified governor models are also not accurate enough. Therefore, a model is needed that can estimate RoCoF and frequency nadir more accurately while maintaining computational speed, and embed them as constraints into FCOPF.

requirement_name: Fast preventive SCOPF for volatile renewables
requirement_text: I need a model that can quickly solve preventive security-constrained OPF (preventive SCOPF) for power systems with high renewable volatility and rapidly changing operating points. In real grid operation, the system must be both economic and satisfy N-1 contingency security constraints. However, SCOPF must consider both the base case and multiple contingency cases, so its problem size is much larger than ordinary OPF, and traditional analytical optimization methods may be too slow for online applications. Although supervised learning and reinforcement learning can accelerate OPF / SCOPF, they may suffer from insufficient constraint satisfaction, inaccurate gradient estimation, or inadequate handling of N-1 security constraints. Therefore, a hybrid model combining the classical SCOPF physical model with data-driven methods is needed, so that it can quickly provide near-optimal online dispatch results while strictly satisfying security constraints.

I need a large-scale AC-OPF convex optimization model suitable for meshed transmission networks. Traditional AC-OPF is non-convex and computationally difficult, making it hard to guarantee global optimality in large-scale systems. Linear approximations such as DC-OPF are fast, but sacrifice accuracy. SOCP-OPF, as a convex relaxation method, has good computational efficiency. However, in meshed transmission networks, traditional SOCP models may fail to correctly recover voltage angles, because voltage angle differences around a closed loop must satisfy cyclic constraints, meaning that the sum of angle differences around a closed loop should be zero. Existing solutions are either computationally expensive or not suitable for large-scale meshed systems. Therefore, an OPF model is needed that can directly consider cyclic angle constraints within the SOCP framework, so that it can maintain SOCP scalability and computational efficiency while improving angle recovery accuracy and the physical consistency of power flow solutions in meshed transmission networks.

I need a stochastic UC-OPF model for an isolated microgrid energy management system (EMS). In isolated microgrids, wind power, photovoltaics, energy storage, diesel generators, and plug-in electric vehicles coexist. Since the system capacity is small and support capability is weak, wind power uncertainty can more easily affect voltage stability and operational security. Existing studies often only add voltage stability constraints to OPF, or fail to treat loading margin as a time- and scenario-dependent variable. They also often do not sufficiently consider the role of PEVs in mitigating microgrid voltage stability problems. Therefore, an EMS model coordinating unit commitment and optimal power flow is needed. It should consider stochastic wind scenarios and jointly determine unit commitment, power dispatch, ESS charging/discharging, PEV charging/discharging, and parking lot capacity, while explicitly guaranteeing voltage stability margin so that isolated microgrids can still operate safely under uncertain renewable energy conditions.

I need a distributed chance-constrained OPF model for multi-area interconnected power grids. Under high wind power penetration, grid dispatch must consider uncertainty, so chance-constrained OPF is needed to ensure that constraints such as line flows, voltages, or supply-demand balance are satisfied with a certain probability. For multi-area interconnected grids, global OPF can improve economy and security, but different regional ISOs are often unwilling to share sensitive information such as generation costs, load data, grid topology, and line parameters, because these data involve commercial interests, regulatory restrictions, and cybersecurity risks. Existing CC-OPF methods are mostly centralized, while existing privacy-preserving methods may cause accuracy loss, high computational cost, integer-only processing, parameter tuning requirements, or convergence issues. Therefore, a distributed and confidential CC-OPF method is needed, so that different regions can cooperatively obtain a dispatch result close or equal to the centralized global optimum without revealing local confidential data.

I need a data-driven model that can quickly solve AC-OPF under different operating patterns / different network topologies. Traditional AC-OPF methods usually model only a fixed operating pattern. When line outage states, network topology, or operating conditions change, the model needs to be adjusted again, which significantly reduces computational efficiency. In real grids, due to renewable energy fluctuations, equipment state changes, and line interruptions, operating patterns are not fixed. Therefore, an AC-OPF solution method is needed that can use historical data to identify operating patterns and use load data plus network topology labels as inputs. In this way, even when the network structure is unknown or changing, the model can quickly predict voltage magnitudes and phase angles, and then obtain the complete OPF solution through power flow calculation.

I need a fast and reliable ACOPF solver for modern smart grids. Due to renewable energy integration, electric vehicle growth, and increasingly unpredictable loads, system operation requires more fine-grained and more frequent ACOPF calculations. However, ACOPF itself is non-convex and NP-hard, and traditional solvers are limited in speed. Although data-driven methods can directly predict OPF solutions from load demand, it is difficult to guarantee both optimality and feasibility, especially because hard constraints, power flow balance constraints, and line constraints may be violated. Therefore, a model combining physics-informed learning and feasibility calibration is needed. It should first use machine learning to predict voltage magnitudes and angles, and then use a calibration algorithm to correct power flow imbalance, so that the final result is close to optimal and satisfies ACOPF physical constraints as much as possible.

I need a physics-informed data-driven OPF model that can replace traditional iterative OPF calculation. Under high renewable penetration and probabilistic analysis scenarios, OPF needs to be solved repeatedly, in large quantities, and in real time. Traditional model-driven methods have high computational burden, while ordinary neural networks require extensive hyperparameter tuning, and directly learning the complex mapping from system operating status to OPF solutions is very difficult. Therefore, a machine learning framework incorporating the physical structure of OPF is needed. It should decompose the complex OPF mapping into multiple stages, gradually learn branch flows, voltages, generator outputs, and objective function values, and use active constraint identification for sample pre-classification, so as to reduce learning complexity, improve generalization ability, and obtain high-quality OPF solutions in a short time.

I need a dispatch model that can be applied to both day-ahead OPF and real-time OPF, in order to handle rapid variations of wind power, solar power, and load within the scheduling period. Traditional DA-OPF is usually calculated based on a one-hour static snapshot, and RT-OPF is usually calculated based on a 5- to 15-minute static snapshot. However, between two consecutive scheduling points, wind power, solar power, and load continue to change, causing additional regulation costs and security risks. Re-optimizing at every shorter time scale would be accurate, but computationally too expensive. Therefore, a method based on “best-fit participation factors” is needed. It should optimize only once at the beginning of the scheduling period, while considering minute-level variations in RT-OPF and 15-minute-level variations in DA-OPF, and include voltage, reactive power, and line flow constraints in all sub-intervals, so that economy and system security can be improved without increasing the dimension of optimization variables.

I need a distributed OPF model for multi-terminal DC distribution grids, used for system-level control and active network management. With large-scale integration of power electronic converters and distributed energy resources, MTDC distribution grids need to update DC voltage setpoints and DER power setpoints at different nodes within short control periods. Different types of DERs have different dispatch objectives: conventional DERs are dispatched according to cost, RES needs to consider curtailment minimization, ESS needs to consider SoC, and controllable loads need to consider curtailment cost. Centralized OPF is not modular enough and has scalability, reliability, and data privacy issues. Therefore, a distributed OPF-for-ANM algorithm based on nodal formulation and ADMM is needed, so that each distributed control unit can use only local information and necessary communication to coordinate RES, ESS, controllable loads, and other DERs, and quickly and scalably realize system-level voltage and power control.

I need an optimization model suitable for distribution system DOPF that can accurately handle discrete control devices such as load tap changers (LTCs). In real distribution grids, LTCs and capacitor banks can only operate in discrete tap positions or states, rather than being continuously adjusted. However, many DOPF models relax integer variables into continuous variables to reduce computational difficulty, and then round the results to obtain tap positions. This approach may lead to infeasible or suboptimal solutions when the system operates close to its limits. With the integration of distributed PV, electric vehicles, storage, and advanced inverters, distribution grid voltage regulation becomes more dynamic. Therefore, a DOPF model is needed that preserves the discrete control characteristics of LTCs while maintaining computational tractability.

I need a model for multi-agent distributed OPF that can maintain D-OPF convergence and feasibility even when communication links are unreliable or interrupted. With the development of DERs, microgrids, and transactive energy markets, centralized OPF may no longer be suitable for future distribution grid operation. Multiple regional agents or microgrid agents need to coordinate through distributed OPF. However, distributed ADMM-type algorithms rely on the exchange of consensus messages or global variables between regions. Once a communication link is lost, some global variables cannot be updated, which may slow convergence, cause results to deviate from global OPF, or make the solution infeasible. Therefore, a D-OPF framework is needed that can predict missing global variables during communication interruptions, for example by using ANN / DFNN to estimate missing voltage phasors or consensus information, so that feasible D-OPF solutions close to the global result can still be obtained under unreliable communication.

I need an OPF model or algorithm for feeder reconfiguration in distribution networks, which selects the on/off status of switches to reduce losses, improve load balancing, or optimize operating conditions. This problem is essentially a mixed-integer nonlinear problem with switch states, and is computationally difficult. Traditional formal methods require long computation times, while branch exchange heuristics may depend on the initial topology and have unstable iteration counts. Therefore, a feeder reconfiguration method based on AC-OPF convex relaxation, especially SOCP relaxation, is needed. It should quickly select the lines to be opened without complex parameter tuning or initialization, and obtain a radial distribution network configuration that is globally optimal or close to optimal as much as possible.

requirement_name: Grid Foundation Model for power systems
requirement_text: I need a Grid Foundation Model (GridFM) for power systems to deal with the large-scale complexity and uncertainty brought by the energy transition. Future power grids will include massive renewable energy, distributed energy resources, electric vehicles, inverter-based devices, climate-driven uncertain loads, and more complex operating scenarios. Traditional simulation and optimization methods will face insufficient computational capability in real-time analysis, large-scale scenario analysis, N-1 / N-2 contingency analysis, OPF, state estimation, and planning. Meanwhile, existing AI models are often trained only for a single task or a single system, with limited transferability. Therefore, a GridFM is needed that can be pre-trained on large amounts of multi-topology, multi-operating-condition, and multimodal grid data, and then adapted to different grids and tasks through small-scale fine-tuning. It is especially needed for accelerating downstream applications such as power flow, optimal power flow, and contingency analysis, while maintaining physical consistency and significantly improving computational speed.

A heuristic OPF model is needed for economic and low-carbon dispatch with high RES penetration, considering stochastic wind power, stochastic photovoltaic power, reserve cost, penalty cost, and carbon tax.

requirement_name: Hybrid UC and OPF correction for PV
requirement_text: A hybrid model combining UC unit commitment scheduling and OPF power flow correction is needed for 24-hour dispatch after PV integration. UC alone may achieve low cost, but it may violate voltage, line, and power flow constraints, so PSO–NR OPF is needed to correct infeasible periods.

A D-OPF model benchmarking framework is needed to compare NLP, SOCP, SDP, LinDistFlow, and other models under different objective functions. The reason is that different D-OPF formulations vary significantly in feasibility, optimality, and scalability, and some relaxation or linear models may produce AC-infeasible solutions.

requirement_name: Wind farm primary voltage control OPF
requirement_text: An OPF model for wind farm primary voltage control is needed, in order to reduce collector grid losses while satisfying PCC reactive power instructions. The model needs to coordinate the reactive power allocation among wind turbines, static capacitor / reactor banks, and OLTCs, avoiding additional losses caused by equal reactive power allocation.

A machine learning-aided fast SCOPF model is needed for obtaining near-optimal solutions that satisfy constraints in large-scale power grids. Pure machine learning can easily violate power flow balance constraints, so this method only predicts voltage magnitudes and angles, and then uses physical network equations to recover the remaining OPF variables.

requirement_name: Multi-period hybrid AC/DC OPF flexibility market
requirement_text: A multi-period hybrid AC/DC-OPF model is needed for flexibility market clearing and TSO-DSO coordination. The model should use SOC-ACOPF on the distribution grid side and DC-OPF on the transmission grid side, while considering flexibility resources such as batteries, flexible loads, load shifting, and load shedding.

requirement_name: Dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF with neural encoding
requirement_text: A model capable of handling dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF is needed. Traditional AC-OPF can consider static constraints, but directly adding dynamic security constraints such as small-signal stability and transient stability makes the problem difficult to solve. Therefore, neural networks are needed to encode the feasible region and transform it into a MILP for solution.

requirement_name: Scalable N-k SCOPF with adversarial robustness
requirement_text: A scalable N-k SCOPF method is needed so that dispatch decisions can withstand multiple simultaneous equipment failures. Traditional N-k SCOPF becomes difficult to solve because contingency combinations explode combinatorially. Therefore, the model should treat contingencies as adversarial attacks and use minimax optimization with implicit differentiation to find more robust dispatch decisions.

An online optimization framework is needed for power systems with high renewable penetration. Wind, photovoltaic generation, and controllable loads fluctuate strongly, while offline optimization based on forecasts or historical data can produce suboptimal, infeasible, or unstable decisions. Therefore, the model should update with real-time operating states through online optimization.

requirement_name: Hybrid AC/DC OPF with VSC-MTDC and renewables
requirement_text: A hybrid AC/DC OPF model is needed that simultaneously considers VSC-MTDC transmission lines and multiple renewable energy sources. The model should satisfy AC/DC network constraints while optimizing fuel cost, emissions, voltage deviation, and active power loss, and it should be suitable for solution with metaheuristic algorithms.

A local and scalable GNN-based ACOPF approximation model is needed. ACOPF is nonconvex and difficult to solve quickly; DCOPF is insufficiently accurate in heavily loaded networks; and ordinary MLPs lack locality and scalability. Therefore, the model should exploit the grid graph structure and train graph neural networks to approximate optimal OPF solutions.

A physics-informed neural network framework is needed so that learning results can still exploit governing physical equations when data are limited. For problems governed by nonlinear physical laws, ordinary deep learning may lack robustness. Therefore, differential equations, conservation laws, and other physics knowledge should be embedded into the loss function to solve or discover physical-system models.

A fast and physics-friendly data-driven AC-OPF model is needed. Traditional AC-OPF is nonlinear and nonconvex, making it hard to solve frequently in real-time operation or large-scale simulation; DC-OPF is fast but may be economically suboptimal and violate AC physics. Therefore, the model should use historical similar states or previous solutions to quickly predict generator active power outputs and voltage setpoints, while using Lagrangian constraint penalties to improve AC-OPF feasibility.

A probabilistically robust AC-OPF model is needed to handle renewable generation and load uncertainty. Wind, photovoltaic generation, and load fluctuations can make deterministic dispatch based on forecasts cause line overloads or constraint violations, while fully robust optimization may be too conservative and costly. Therefore, a chance-constrained or probabilistically robust AC-OPF is needed to minimize generation cost while controlling constraint-violation risk within a specified small probability and maintaining generation and transmission security.

requirement_name: Real-time OPF with Lagrangian reinforcement learning
requirement_text: A real-time OPF model is needed that can quickly produce economic and constraint-satisfying dispatch decisions when renewable generation and random load change rapidly. Traditional OPF is too slow for real-time fluctuations; reduced-iteration methods may be suboptimal; and supervised learning methods often do not explicitly guarantee power-flow, line-capacity, and ramping constraints. Therefore, a Lagrangian reinforcement-learning RT-OPF method is needed to output generator active power and voltage setpoints in continuous action space while balancing cost minimization and constraint satisfaction.

A real-time decision model is needed for sequential security-constrained OPF. High renewable penetration and load fluctuations make grid operation time-varying, and intertemporal constraints such as ramping limits mean current dispatch affects future feasibility and long-term reward. AC models are nonconvex and real environments contain parameter errors. Therefore, the model should combine reinforcement-learning fast decision capability with optimization-based safety-constraint handling, use a safety layer to correct unsafe actions, and support coordinated active and reactive dispatch.

requirement_name: Reserve-constrained AC-OPF with energy and reserve co-optimization
requirement_text: A reserve-constrained AC-OPF model is needed to jointly optimize energy dispatch and reserve allocation. Random load, renewable fluctuations, and equipment failures require both economic dispatch and reserve support. Sequential energy-then-reserve allocation or simplified ED/DC methods may ignore AC networks, reactive reserve, voltage, and line-flow constraints. Therefore, the model should jointly represent active/reactive dispatch, multiple reserve types, regional reserve requirements, line flows, and voltage constraints under the full AC network and solve large-scale RCOPF efficiently.

A scalable large-scale multi-period SCOPF model is needed. Real grid dispatch must jointly consider multiple time steps, unit commitment, reserves, ramping, post-contingency security constraints, and AC power-flow constraints, leading to millions of continuous variables, integer variables, and nonlinear nonconvex constraints. Traditional SCOPF or commercial tools may not solve directly under strict time limits, while DC-OPF ignores voltage and reactive power. Therefore, decomposition, linearization, constraint relaxation, sequential optimization, or hybrid solvers are needed to obtain high-quality, feasible, near-AC-model solutions within limited time.

requirement_name: Multi-period OPF for community storage and PV sizing
requirement_text: A multi-period OPF model is needed for sizing and placing community energy storage and photovoltaic capacity in low-voltage distribution networks. With high PV penetration, the local grid needs to balance supply and demand, improve self-sufficiency, and reduce exchange with the external grid. CES capacity, installation location, PV capacity, self-sufficiency, network losses, and power-flow constraints are coupled. Therefore, the model should jointly optimize PV capacity, CES capacity, and CES location while considering network losses, grid import/export power, and community self-sufficiency under different cost scenarios.

requirement_name: Unbalanced three-phase OPF for smart distribution grids
requirement_text: A three-phase unbalanced OPF model is needed for smart distribution-grid DMS applications. Traditional OPF is mainly designed for transmission systems and cannot accurately represent three-phase imbalance, single-phase loads, single-phase distributed generation, and micro-generation units in distribution grids. Smart distribution grids need near-real-time voltage regulation, reactive dispatch, overload mitigation, load control, and security analysis. Therefore, a TOPF method based on unbalanced three-phase power flow is needed to coordinate active load curtailment, reactive redispatch, voltage control, and loss minimization while satisfying security constraints on each phase.

requirement_name: DR-based AC-OPF with flexible-load aggregators and uncertainty
requirement_text: A demand-response-based AC-OPF scheduling model is needed that combines flexible-load aggregators and uncertainty handling. EVs, HVACs, large flexible loads, and storage can participate in demand response for peak shaving, cost reduction, and renewable utilization improvement, but existing work often considers only active-load adjustment or a single flexible-load type and rarely considers EV/HVAC aggregators, user comfort, load-forecast errors, and DER uncertainty together. Therefore, a DR-based AC-OPF model should jointly schedule large flexible loads, EV aggregators, and HVAC aggregators while satisfying AC power-flow, generator, line, and voltage constraints, minimizing cost and peak load, and improving user revenue, convenience, and RES utilization.
